title: From Hollywood studios to *digital products*.
intro: How cinematic vision shapes the way I design interfaces — dimensional thinking, visual storytelling and technical precision.
quote: Every pixel tells a story, every interaction creates an emotion. My VFX background taught me that the magic happens in the details — the subtle lighting that guides the eye, the precise timing that creates anticipation, the dimensional thinking that turns flat interfaces into immersive experiences.

timeline.title: The transition
timeline.text: Saw the chance to apply cinematic vision to digital experiences and pursued formal UX education at IIIT Bangalore, building a hybrid skill set.

timeline.title: VFX studio work
timeline.text: Honed technical precision on major Hollywood productions including Secret Headquarters, Pinocchio and Ant-Man, specialising in 3D modelling.

timeline.title: Product design
timeline.text: Graduated with a perfect CGPA and now bring dimensional thinking to interfaces that are clear, intuitive and tell a story — most recently at Baron Tech Labs.

why.title: Dimensional thinking
why.text: VFX means understanding how things sit in 3D space, how light hits a surface and how movement creates emotion. In UI that becomes spatial hierarchy, visual depth and interaction choreography.

why.title: Technical precision
why.text: Film work demands systematic workflows where every frame serves the story. The same discipline makes interfaces that are both beautiful and functional.

why.title: Where it's heading
why.text: As interfaces move toward AR/VR and spatial computing, designers who understand 3D space, lighting and cinematic principles will build the most compelling experiences.
